title: חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון

paragraphs: Chananyah ben Chizkiyah ben Garon, remembered for good: Mishnah Shabbat 1:4. He lived in the Temple period and wrote Megillat Taanit. Yuchasin, in its sequence of generations, suggests that he did not write all of it, as appears in Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1: R. Yehudah ben Shamua, R. Meir's student, annulled a persecution decree, and this is in Megillat Taanit. He cites Shabbat, chapter 1, and the end of Megillat Taanit for the tradition that the company of R. Elazar ben Chananyah ben Chizkiyah ben Garon wrote the scroll. [Shabbat names Chananyah and his company.] He had a learned son named R. Elazar. So too Sifrei, end of Tetze, and Mekhilta, Yitro. Semachot, chapter 6: an incident with Elazar, Chananyah, and Chizkiyah ben Garon—I think it should read Elazar ben Chananyah ben Chizkiyah ben Garon—who lost a Torah scroll bought for one hundred maneh. He prayed in the Temple and found it. Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel went up to visit him, and in his house they decreed eighteen matters: end of chapter 1 of Shabbat, 13b. He brought up three hundred jars of wine [the cited Bavli passages read oil] and expounded the Book of Ezekiel, and is remembered for good: HaTekhelet, Menachot 45a, near the end; Chagigah 13a has Chanina ben Chizkiyah [the retrieved Chagigah reads Chananyah; Menachot reads Chanina]; Niddah 43.
